title: Hemoglobin A1c
content: Normal below 5.7 percent. Prediabetes 5.7 to 6.4 percent. Diabetes diagnosed at 6.5 percent or above. A target of 7 percent suits most adults on treatment.

title: Thyroid stimulating hormone
content: Reference range 0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L. A raised TSH with low free T4 indicates primary hypothyroidism. A suppressed TSH suggests hyperthyroidism.

title: Serum potassium
content: Reference range 3.5 to 5.1 mmol/L. Above 5.5 is hyperkalaemia and above 6.5 is an emergency needing ECG and urgent treatment. Below 3.5 is hypokalaemia.

title: International normalized ratio
content: Reference range 0.8 to 1.2 off treatment. The therapeutic INR on warfarin is 2.0 to 3.0, or 2.5 to 3.5 with a mechanical mitral valve.

title: Estimated glomerular filtration rate
content: Normal is 90 mL/min/1.73 m2 or above. Stage 3 chronic kidney disease is 30 to 59. Below 15 indicates kidney failure. Used to dose metformin and anticoagulants.

title: High-sensitivity troponin
content: Above the 99th percentile upper reference limit suggests myocardial injury. Repeat at zero and one to three hours and interpret the delta against the assay algorithm.

title: LDL cholesterol
content: Optimal below 100 mg/dL. Very high risk patients target below 55 mg/dL. Recheck four to twelve weeks after starting a statin.

title: Serum creatinine
content: Reference range 0.6 to 1.3 mg/dL in adults. A rise of 0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours defines acute kidney injury.

title: Blood lactate
content: Normal below 2 mmol/L. Above 2 suggests hypoperfusion and above 4 mmol/L is a severity marker in sepsis.

title: D-dimer
content: Below 500 ng/mL FEU rules out venous thromboembolism when pretest probability is low. Age-adjusted cut-off applies over 50 years.
